ed.faceSub: Drop an image, pick one from Kataki’s set, or leave it. They get an initial until you decide.
ed.name: Name
ed.nameHint: What you call them. You can change it later.
ed.nameErr: Give them a name. It’s the one thing Kataki can’t guess.
ed.optional: Optional · add any of these whenever
ed.aboutSub: What anyone would see. Two or three lines is plenty.
ed.aboutHint: Everyone who meets them could notice this. Characters read it every turn.
ed.tagsHint: Up to three, with commas between.
ed.talkSub: Two sample lines. This does more than anything else here.
ed.secretSub: Something only they know. It changes how they answer.
ed.secretHint: Only this character knows it. They never say it unless the story earns it.
ed.relsSub: Who they already know, and how they feel about them.
ed.placesSub: Pick from your World, or write a new one.

ed.modelSub: Leave it and they use the defaults in Settings.
ed.modelHint: Only models that are connected now are listed.

cr.cancelled: The payment was cancelled. Nothing was charged.
cr.waiting: The {amount} payment is still going through. Your balance updates when it does.
ac.balanceSub: What is left to spend on replies. Each one costs what the model charges.
si.title: Sign in to Kataki
si.name: Your name
si.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. A few plain words in a row is a good one.
si.sentBody: If {email} can be used here, a link is on its way. Open it on this device to finish. It works for one hour.
si.forgotBody: Say which email the account uses, and a link to choose a new password is sent there.
si.forgotSent: If {email} has an account, a link to choose a new password is on its way. It works for 15 minutes.
si.linkBody: No password needed: a link is sent to your email, and it signs you in once.
si.linkSent: If {email} has an account, a sign-in link is on its way. It works once, for 10 minutes.
si.resetDone: Your password is changed, and every device was signed out. Sign in with the new one.
si.magicBody: You asked for a sign-in link. Press the button to finish on this device.
si.e.link: That link has been used or is too old. Ask for a new one.
si.codeBody: Open your authenticator app and type the 6-digit code it shows for Kataki.
si.backupBody: Type one of the backup codes you saved when you turned this on. Each works once.
si.trust: Don’t ask again on this device for 30 days
si.e.code: That code is not right. Check the app and try again.
si.e.codeLate: That took too long. Sign in again to get a new try.
am.title: Signing in
am.usernameNone: None. A short name you can sign in with instead of your email.
am.usernameIs: {name}. You can sign in with it instead of your email.
am.usernameBody: A short name that is yours alone. You can sign in with it, and it is what others would see if profiles are ever shared.
am.usernameHint: 3 to 30 lowercase letters, numbers or underscores.
am.e.taken: Someone already has that username. Try another.
am.e.name: That username cannot be used. Try another.
am.backupNone: None. A second address that also hears when something about your account changes.
am.backupOn: {email} also hears when something about your account changes.
am.backupWaiting: {email} has a link to open before it is used.
am.backupBody: A second address that gets a copy of the notices about your account: a changed password, a new email, two-step sign-in turned off. It cannot be used to sign in.
am.backupSent: A link is on its way to {email}. It is used once that link is opened.
am.passwordSet: Set. Changing it signs every other place out.
am.passwordNone: None yet. You signed up with another service; use “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in screen to set one.
am.withSub: Use your {name} account to sign in here too.
am.emailBody: Two mails follow: one to your current address to approve the change, then one to the new address to confirm it. Nothing changes until both are opened.
am.emailSent: Check {email} first: the change waits for your approval there.
am.passwordBody: Every other place you are signed in is signed out.
am.e.other: That did not work. Check what you typed and try again.
am.fresh: To be sure it is you, this needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes. Sign out, sign back in, and try again.
am.e.unlink: That is the only way into this account. Set a password or link another service first.
lv.title: Your data, and leaving
lv.exportSub: What the service holds about you: your email, how you sign in, where you are signed in, and every charge. Your stories and characters export from Data and privacy.
lv.deleteSub: Everything goes after 14 days. Until then, signing in and choosing to stay undoes it.
lv.deleteBody: You are signed out everywhere now. In 14 days the account is removed for good.
lv.whatBody: Every story, character, place and picture in your library online, your sign-in, and your balance. Records of what was charged are kept, as the law requires, without your name or email. Export the library first if you want to keep it.
lv.goingBody: {name}, your account is set to be deleted on {date}. Nothing has been removed yet.
lv.go: Sign out and let it go
si.e.passkey: That passkey did not work here. Sign in another way, then add this device under Settings › Account.
pk.title: Passkeys
pk.note: Sign in with this device itself: your fingerprint, your face or its PIN. Nothing to remember, and nothing to steal from a website.
pk.addSub: Your device asks you to confirm it is you. It counts as both steps of two-step sign-in.
pk.added: This device can now sign you in.
pk.e: The passkey could not be added. Try again, or use another device.
cl.title: Cloud
cl.note: A copy of this library on your Kataki online account: a way back if this computer is lost, and a way to carry it to another one. Nothing is sent until you say so.
cl.connectSub: Link this computer to your account to save this library there.
cl.holds: {stories, plural, one {# story} other {# stories}}, {characters, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}, {places, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}, {plots, plural, one {# plot} other {# plots}}
cl.offline: Connected, but Kataki online is not answering
cl.offlineSub: Try again in a moment. Nothing here has changed.
cl.ahead: The cloud copy has changed since this library last met it.
cl.nothing: Nothing is saved in the cloud yet.
cl.tooBig: This library is larger than the cloud takes ({mb} MB).
cl.e: The cloud could not be reached.
cl.freeSub: Up to {holds}. A larger library is kept for {price} per GB a month, from your balance.
cl.past: This library is past that, so keeping it is charged daily while you have credit.
cl.needsCredit: This library is past the free limit and your balance is empty, so it was not saved. Add credit on Kataki online, or save a smaller library. What is already in the cloud is kept.
cl.clashTitle: The cloud copy is not the one this library came from
cl.clashBody: It was saved {when} from {device}: {holds}. Saving now would replace it.
cl.clashGone: Something else is saved there. Saving now would replace it.
cl.downBody: Kataki restarts, and this library becomes the cloud copy. What is here now is kept as a backup first (Backups, above), so it can be had back.
cl.linkBody: Your browser has opened Kataki online. Sign in there if asked, check the code matches, and approve.
cl.linkExpired: That took too long, or was turned down. Close this and connect again.
cl.waiting: Waiting for you to approve it…
ln.title: Connect a computer?
ln.body: “{computer}” is asking to save its library to your account, {account}, and bring it down again.
ln.check: Only say yes if Kataki on your own computer is showing this same code right now.
ln.doneBody: Go back to Kataki on your computer. You can remove this computer any time under Settings › Account.
ln.goneBody: It may have been used or be too old. Ask for a new one in Kataki on your computer.
dv.title: Linked computers
dv.note: Computers that can save their library to this account and bring it down.
se.title: Where you’re signed in
se.note: Every browser and device with this account open.
ts.title: Two-step sign-in
ts.note: A second step when you sign in: a code from an app on your phone. Someone with only your password stays out.
ts.isOn: Asked for when you sign in, whichever way you do it.
ts.isOff: Off. Your password, a sign-in link or another service is enough.
ts.onBody: You need an authenticator app on your phone, like Google Authenticator, Authy, or the one in your password manager. First, your password.
ts.onBodyNoPassword: You need an authenticator app on your phone, like Google Authenticator, Authy, or the one in your password manager.
ts.offBodyNoPassword: Signing in will need only one step again.
ts.scan: Scan this with your authenticator app, or type the key in by hand. Then type the 6-digit code the app shows.
ts.qrAlt: A QR code to scan with an authenticator app
ts.codesBody: If you lose your phone, one of these gets you in. Each works once. Keep them somewhere safe: they are not shown again.
ts.offBody: Signing in will need only one step again. Your password, to be sure it is you.
ts.newCodesBody: The old codes stop working. Your password, to be sure it is you.
ts.e.password: That did not work. Check your password.
ts.e.code: That code is not right. Check the app and try again.
si.noAccount: You don’t have a Kataki account with that sign-in yet. Tick “I am 18 or older”, then press the same button below to make one.
si.e.tick: Tick “I am 18 or older” first, then press the button again.
si.e.back: That did not finish (code: {code}). Try again, and if it keeps happening tell us the code.
si.e.wrong: Those do not match an account.
si.e.email: That does not look like an email address.
si.e.short: That password is too short. Use at least 12 characters.
si.e.long: That password is too long. Use at most 128 characters.
si.e.breached: That password has appeared in a leak of stolen passwords, so it is not safe anywhere. Choose another.
si.e.slow: Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.
si.e.adult: Kataki online is for people aged 18 or older.
si.e.other: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
pf.what: A profile is a name and a folder
pf.whatBody: Each profile keeps its own stories, characters, places and settings in its own folder. Profiles on this computer share downloaded models and saved keys, and anyone who can open the folder can read it.
pf.addSub: Start an empty library in a new folder, or choose a folder that already holds one.
pf.newBody: Name it, then choose its folder. A folder on this computer is safest: folders that sync, like OneDrive or Dropbox, can damage a library.
pf.name: Name
pf.forgetBody: It comes off this list and nothing is deleted. Its library stays in {folder}, and you can add it again.
pf.ask: Ask which profile when Kataki starts
pf.askSub: Otherwise it opens the one you used last. A profile with a PIN always asks.
pf.movedBody: The old copy is still in {folder}. Kataki no longer uses it.
pf.pinBody: Kataki asks for it before this profile opens. It keeps the profile out of casual reach on this computer; it does not lock the files themselves, which anyone who can open the folder can still read.
pf.pinGone: {name} no longer asks for a PIN.
pf.pinWrong: That is not the PIN it has now.
bd.title: Badges
bd.body: Earned from what you make and write here. They are for you: nobody else sees them, and nothing is lost by ignoring them.
bd.toggle: Show badges, and say when I earn one
bd.new: {n, plural, one {Badge earned: {name}} other {# badges earned: {name} and more}}
pc.title: Your profile
pc.blank: A name, a picture and a few words about you. Only you see this.
pc.editBody: This is you, not someone you play. It stays in your library and goes where the library goes.
pc.name: Your name
pc.bioHint: {n, plural, one {# character left} other {# characters left}}
pc.accentHint: It rings your picture on the card.
g.note: How Kataki behaves when it opens and while it runs.
g.openToSub: Go straight back into the last scene, or stop at Home first.
g.historySub: Lets you go back to an earlier take or edit days later. Costs disk space.
g.updatesSub: Kataki asks one version endpoint for a number. No account, no identifier, nothing about your stories.
g.startupSub: Opens quietly to the tray when you sign in.
g.closeSub: What the × does. The tray icon can always quit.
g.storiesNote: What a new story starts with. Each story can change all of it in Story settings.
g.modeSub: Auto reads how you write. Say, Do, Whisper, Think and Narrate override it.
g.speedSub: How a reply arrives on screen once it’s written.
g.content.gentleSub: For any audience: no sexual content, and violence stays brief and off the page.
g.content.matureSub: Romance, violence and dark themes when the story leads there; sex fades to black.
g.content.explicitSub: Nothing is faded out: sex and graphic violence are written in full when the story leads there, between adults.
g.avoidSub: Topics the characters steer away from, whatever the level. Separate them with commas.
g.adultBody: Choose this only if you are 18 or older. No level ever allows sexual content involving anyone under 18.
ap.note: The Sky has two themes. Inside a story it is always golden hour.
ap.motionSub: Clouds crossfade instead of parting, stars stay still, the caret stops blinking.
ap.starsSub: Purely decorative. Turning them off leaves the gradient.
ap.fontSub: What characters’ lines and story names are set in.
la.note: The interface language. What your characters speak is up to them and the model.
la.mirrorSub: The rail moves to the right and arrows flip. Your own writing keeps its direction.
la.clockSub: Story times stay relative either way. This is for “Played 2 hours ago” and exact times.
me.note: How much of a person a character is allowed to be. These are defaults; any character can change them.
me.fadeSub: Sharp, then hazy, then gone, by story time. Slower means more consistent and slower replies.
me.wrongSub: A hazy memory can come back slightly changed, the way people misremember.
me.doubtSub: If what you say contradicts what they hold, they may say so instead of going along.
me.thinkingSub: More thinking is slower and more in character.
me.hearingSub: Whether someone in the room hears a whisper, and whether someone who left hears anything.
me.replyLengthSub: Every reply leans this way; a story can ask for more or less.
